primaryText: María se casó con algún estudiante del departamento de lingüística.
translation: María married a linguistics student.
comment: Conveys that the speaker does not know which student. Repeated as (19) and (55a).

primaryText: María se casó con algún estudiante del departamento de lingüística: en concreto con Pedro.
translation: María married a linguistics student, namely Pedro.

primaryText: María se casó con un estudiante del departamento de lingüística: en concreto con Pedro.
translation: María married a linguistics student, namely Pedro.

primaryText: Pedro piensa que María se casó con algún estudiante del departamento de lingüística.
translation: Pedro thinks that María married a linguistics student.

readings.name: wide scope: a particular student Pedro thinks María married, the speaker does not know who
narrow scope: Pedro is uncertain about the identity of the student

primaryText: Mi coche tiene algún abollón.
comment: Strongly suggests that the speaker does not know how many dents her car has. Repeated as (74a).

primaryText: Mary musste irgendeinen Arzt heiraten.
translation: Mary had to marry a doctor.
comment: Kratzer 2005, p. 129; repeated as (12). Any doctor in the domain was a permitted option.

primaryText: Juan tiene que estar en alguna habitación de la casa.
translation: Juan must be in a room of the house.
context: Hide and seek. María, Juan, and Pedro are playing hide-and-seek in their country house. Juan is hiding. Pedro is sure that Juan is inside the house, and sure that Juan is not in the bathroom or in the kitchen; as far as he knows, Juan could be in any of the other rooms.
comment: Felicitous only if Juan is not in the same room in all of the speaker's epistemic alternatives; Pedro can utter it in the hide-and-seek scenario although not all rooms are possibilities. Repeated as (14) and (56a).

primaryText: A: Juan tiene que estar en alguna habitación de la casa. B: ¿En cuál?
translation: A: Juan must be in a room of the house. B: In which one?

primaryText: Juan tiene que estar en alguna habitación de la casa, en concreto en la cocina.
translation: Juan is in a room of the house, namely in the kitchen.

primaryText: A: Juan tiene que estar en una habitación de la casa. B: ¿En cuál?
translation: A: Juan must be in a room of the house. B: In which one?

primaryText: Juan tiene que estar en una habitación de la casa, en concreto en la cocina.
translation: Juan must be in a room of the house, namely in the kitchen.

primaryText: A: Mr. X tiene que estar en alguna parada de la línea azul. B: ¡No! Mr. X. tiene que estar en alguna parada de la línea verde.
translation: A: Mr. X has to be in a blue line stop. B: No! Mr. X. has to be in a green line stop.
context: Board game: find in which stop of the Boston subway system (blue, red, green, orange lines) Mr. X is hiding. Player B knows that Mr. X is not in the blue, red, or orange lines, but player A thinks he is in a station of the blue line.
comment: B's remark is appropriate and true although B knows that some green line stops (the transfer stations) are excluded: no Free Choice component.

primaryText: A: Juan está en la cocina. B: ¡No, Juan está en el baño! A: Bueno, Juan está en alguna habitación. Eso seguro, ¿no?
translation: A: Juan is in the kitchen. B: No, Juan is in the bathroom! A: Well, Juan is in some room. We are sure of that, aren't we?
comment: Adapted from Condoravdi 2005. Each speaker knows where Juan is; the Modal Variation component targets the common ground.

primaryText: Juan puede estar en alguna habitación de la casa.
translation: Juan may be in a room of the house.
context: The hide-and-seek situation, but now, according to what Pedro knows, if Juan is in the house he could only be in the bathroom.
comment: Deviant when there is only one room where Juan might be. Repeated as (60a) without the scenario.

primaryText: Juan puede estar en una habitación de la casa.
translation: Juan may be in a room of the house.
context: The hide-and-seek situation, but now, according to what Pedro knows, if Juan is in the house he could only be in the bathroom.

primaryText: Puedes coger cualquiera de las cartas de esta baraja.
translation: You can take any of the cards in this deck.
comment: True only if the addressee is allowed to take any card.

primaryText: Juan puede estar en cualquier parte de la casa.
translation: Juan may be anywhere in the house.
context: Hide-and-seek; Juan is hiding. Pedro is convinced that Juan is not in the bathroom or in the kitchen, but for all Pedro knows Juan could be in any of the other rooms of the house, or even outside (say, in the barn).

primaryText: Juan puede estar en alguna parte de la casa.
translation: Juan may be in a part of the house.
context: Hide-and-seek; Juan is hiding. Pedro is convinced that Juan is not in the bathroom or in the kitchen, but for all Pedro knows Juan could be in any of the other rooms of the house, or even outside (say, in the barn).

primaryText: El departamento puede contratar a cualquiera de los candidatos que han solicitado el puesto.
translation: The department can hire any of the candidates that have applied to the position.
context: The department of linguistics is hiring a new professor. Several candidates have applied, but some of them don't have a Ph.D. According to University policies, only candidates with a Ph.D. can be hired.

primaryText: El departamento puede contratar a alguno de los candidatos que han solicitado el puesto.
translation: The department can hire one of the candidates that have applied to the position.
context: The department of linguistics is hiring a new professor. Several candidates have applied, but some of them don't have a Ph.D. According to University policies, only candidates with a Ph.D. can be hired.

primaryText: jo bhii laRkii mehnat kar rahii hai vo safal hogii
translation: The girl who is making an effort will be successful.

primaryText: There's a lot of garlic in whatever (it is that) Arlo is cooking.
Unless there's a lot of garlic in whatever Arlo is cooking, I will eat out tonight.

readings.name: Unless I don't know what Arlo is cooking and there is a lot of garlic in what he is cooking, I will eat out tonight

primaryText: It is not true that there's a lot of garlic in whatever Arlo is cooking.

readings.name: the speaker doesn't know what Arlo is cooking, but the thing Arlo is cooking has a lot of garlic in it

primaryText: No es verdad que Juan salga con alguna chica del departamento de lingüística.
translation: Juan is not dating any of the girls in the linguistics department.

readings.name: Juan is not dating any girl in the department
the speaker knows which girl Juan is dating

comment: No contradiction arises, so the modal component does not project; local accommodation would wrongly allow the speaker to know which girl. Repeated as (43).

primaryText: The mathematician who proved Goldbach's conjecture is not a woman, because nobody has proved Goldbach's conjecture!
comment: A version of an example in von Fintel 2003.

primaryText: Sheila says that Chuck, a confirmed psychopath, is fit to watch the kids.
comment: The paper cites (38) from Potts (2007), 'Conventional implicatures, a distinguished class of meanings', in The Oxford handbook of linguistic interfaces.

primaryText: Sheila believes that Chuck, a psychopath, should be locked up. But Chuck is not a psychopath.
comment: The paper prints # before the second sentence and cites (38) from Potts (2007), 'Conventional implicatures, a distinguished class of meanings', in The Oxford handbook of linguistic interfaces.

primaryText: Juan sabe que María se casó con algún estudiante del departamento. Él no sabe con quién, ¡pero yo sí!
translation: Juan knows that María married a student in the department. He doesn't know who, but I do!

primaryText: Llevamos unos cuantos días intentando averiguar quién es el nuevo amor de María. Todo lo que Juan sabe es que María sale con algún estudiante del departamento. ¡Pero yo ya sé con quién sale María!
translation: We've been trying to find out for days who María's new love is. All Juan knows is that María is going out with some student of the department or other. But I know who María is going out with!
comment: The paper prints averigüar.

primaryText: Edna, a fearless leader, started the descent.
comment: The paper cites (41) from Potts (2007), 'Conventional implicatures, a distinguished class of meanings', in The Oxford handbook of linguistic interfaces.

primaryText: Edna, a fearless leader, started the descent. In fact, Edna is not a fearless leader.
comment: The paper marks the example with ♯ and cites (41) from Potts (2007), 'Conventional implicatures, a distinguished class of meanings', in The Oxford handbook of linguistic interfaces.

primaryText: María se casó con algún estudiante de lingüística. De hecho, sé exactamente con quién.
translation: María married a linguistics student. In fact, I know exactly who!

primaryText: Pedro duda que Juan salga con alguna chica del departamento de lingüística.
translation: Pedro doubts that Juan is dating any girl in the linguistics department.
comment: The paper prints departmento.

primaryText: Edna, a fearless leader, started the descent, and Edna is a fearless leader.
The king of France is bald, and there is a king of France.
Jim kissed Kim passionately, and Kim was kissed.
María sale con algún estudiante del departamento de lingüística, pero no sé con quién.
translation: María is dating some student in the linguistics department, but I don't know who.

primaryText: Juan compró un libro que resultó ser el más caro de la librería.
translation: Juan bought a book that happened to be the most expensive one in the bookstore.

primaryText: Juan compró algún libro que resultó ser el más caro de la librería.
translation: Juan bought a book that happened to be the most expensive one in the store.

primaryText: Pedro contrató a un candidato que era el más incompetente de los que se presentaron.
translation: Pedro hired a candidate that was the most incompetent of the ones that applied.

primaryText: Pedro contrató a algún candidato que era el más incompetente de los que se presentaron.
translation: Pedro hired a candidate that was be the most incompetent of the ones that applied.
comment: The translation is as printed, with 'was be'.

primaryText: A: We know that Juan must be in the house, but where in the house is he? B: (He is) either in the bathroom or in the living room.
context: Hide and seek. María, Juan, and Pedro are playing hide-and-seek in their country house. Juan is hiding. Pedro is sure that Juan is inside the house, and sure that Juan is not in the bathroom or in the kitchen; as far as he knows, Juan could be in any of the other rooms.

readings.name: Juan might be in the bathroom
Juan might be in the living room
there is no other room of the house where Juan might be

comment: B's answer is understood as an exhaustive enumeration (Zimmermann 2001); the inferences are (63a–c).

primaryText: A: We know that Juan must be in the house, but where in the house is he? B: Está en alguna de estas dos habitaciones: en el baño o en la salita.
translation: B: He is in one of these two rooms: in the bathroom or in the living room.
comment: Algún with an explicit two-room domain; A concludes that Juan can only be in those two rooms.

primaryText: Hay alguna mosca en la sopa.
comment: At least one fly in the soup, but the speaker is not sure how many.

primaryText: Juanito todavía tiene algún diente de leche.
No es verdad que haya alguna mosca en la sopa.
comment: Just means that the soup is fly-less.

primaryText: Hay alguna mosca en la sopa... De hecho, hay tres.
Hay alguna mosca en la sopa, pero no sé cuántas.
Hay moscas en la sopa.
comment: The competitor that rules out a belief in more than one fly.

primaryText: Hay tres moscas en la sopa.
comment: The competitor that rules out knowledge of the exact number.

primaryText: Vino algún estudiante.

readings.name: the speaker does not know who the student was (uniqueness assumed)
the speaker does not know how many students came (uniqueness not assumed)

primaryText: Da ist irgendeine Fliege in der Suppe.
comment: Can only mean that there is exactly one fly, which the speaker cannot identify; hence odd.

primaryText: I've been stung by some wasp.
comment: Strawson 1974, pp. 110–111: the suggestion of a possible identification of the wasp seems absurd.

primaryText: Juan wohnt mit irgendwelchen Studenten aus dem Institut zusammen.
translation: Juan lives with some students from the department.

primaryText: Juan vive con algunos estudiantes del departamento.
translation: Juan lives with some students from the department.
comment: The paper prints departmento.

primaryText: Juan wohnt mit irgendwelchen Studenten aus dem Institut zusammen und zwar mit Peter und Sally.
translation: Juan lives with some students in the department, namely Peter and Sally.
comment: Irgendwelche conveys ignorance about the group, as expected.

primaryText: Juan vive con algunos estudiantes en el departamento, en concreto Pedro y María.
translation: Juan lives with some students in the department, namely Pedro and María.
comment: Algunos does not convey ignorance about the group, unexpectedly. The paper prints departmento.

primaryText: Subí a una montaña más alta de Massachusetts.
translation: I climbed a tallest mountain in Massachusetts.
comment: Heim 1991; Sauerland 2003a, b; Percus 2006.

primaryText: Subí a una montaña que es la más alta de Massachusetts.
translation: I climbed a mountain that is the tallest of Massachusetts.

primaryText: Hay un país que podría desaparecer si no se le presta ayuda para combatir la enfermedad.
translation: There is a (sub-Saharan) country that could disappear if it is not offered help to fight the disease.
context: Question asked by reader in on-line interview: In which areas of the world is the AIDS problem the worst? Answer by doctor: In sub-Saharan Africa, undoubtlessly ...
comment: Adapted from Martí 2009: un can range over a domain made salient by the context.

primaryText: He might be in the bedroom.
comment: Need not trigger an exhaustivity inference, though it may with certain intonations.

primaryText: Puede estar en una habitación de la casa.
translation: He might be in a room of the house.

primaryText: Da ist irgendein Gewürz an der Suppe, das ich nicht mag.
translation: There is some spice in the soup that I don't like.
comment: Due to an anonymous reviewer: no commitment to exactly one spice.

primaryText: Hay una especia en la sopa que no me gusta.
translation: There is some spice in the soup that I don't like.
